subject: Learning Methods
title: The All-Nighter Myth
description: A quick, practical guide to The All-Nighter Myth.

hook.text: The All-Nighter Myth: effective learning usually works differently from what feels easiest.

buildup.text: The All-Nighter Myth sets up the method, the mechanism, and the learning tradeoff.

discovery.text: Without sleep, the hippocampus can't transfer that crammed material to long-term memory. Within days, all of it's gone.

twist.text: The all-nighter also impairs exam performance. Even with perfect knowledge, tired brains make more errors in recall.

climax.text: If you must choose: sleep beats cramming. A rested brain retrieves existing knowledge better than a tired brain recalls.

punchline.text: Sleep beats cramming. A rested brain recalls more.

quiz.question: Why do all-nighters impair exam performance beyond memory?
options: Fatigue impairs recall accuracy and reasoning even for known material
Exam rooms are too cold for tired students to concentrate
